report.answer_text:
GPT-5 is OpenAI's flagship AI model. OpenAI announced it on August 7, 2025, calling it its best AI system yet. It is now the default model in ChatGPT.
Main new features
A unified system with a router. GPT-5 combines a smart, efficient model for most questions, a deeper reasoning model ("GPT-5 thinking") for harder problems, and a real-time router that decides which to use. This removes the old split between OpenAI's flagship models and its o-series reasoning models. Users no longer have to choose between them.
Better reasoning and efficiency. In OpenAI's evaluations, GPT-5 with thinking beat o3 while using 50–80% fewer output tokens.
Fewer hallucinations. With web search on, GPT-5's responses were about 45% less likely to contain a factual error than GPT-4o's. When thinking, they were about 80% less likely than o3's.
Stronger coding and agentic tasks. OpenAI calls it its strongest coding model to date. It is also better at agentic tasks generally, because improved tool intelligence lets it chain actions together more reliably. OpenAI also highlighted its writing and health capabilities.
Multimodal input. The GPT-5 models take text and image inputs. Native video and audio input was not part of the initial release.
New developer controls in the API.
The reasoning_effort parameter gained a "minimal" setting for faster answers.
Custom tools let the model call tools with plaintext instead of JSON.
A verbosity parameter controls response length, and Context-Free Grammars enforce specific output formats.
Three API sizes. The API offers gpt-5, gpt-5-mini and gpt-5-nano, so developers can trade off performance, cost and latency.
Reception: MIT Technology Review described it as more of a smoother, more seamless user experience than a dramatic leap. It compared Sam Altman's "Retina display" analogy to that effect.
Some sources I found also list a 1M+ token context window, built-in memory and native audio. One came from a third-party blog and the other from the OpenAI pages I checked, so treat those as unconfirmed. The search results also mention later versions, such as GPT-5.1 and beyond. I didn't verify details on those.
